cases.answer: Use ResizeObserver because it is faster than a window resize listener and fires before the browser paints anything.

cases.answer: A window resize event only fires when the viewport changes. A sidebar collapsing or a web font loading can resize a card while the window stays the same size. ResizeObserver reports that element's own size change.

cases.answer: If teams release on their own schedules and the shared parts are stable, I'd publish a versioned package with semantic versioning, changelogs and a deprecation policy, so each team upgrades when it is ready. If the teams are tightly coupled and change things together, a monorepo makes atomic changes easier, but it needs clear ownership and CI that only runs the affected suites.

Importing still executes the top-level statements outside the guard. The guard keeps the command-line startup from running on import, while running the file directly executes that block. Reusable functions can be imported independently.

Queries and their should assertions run again until success or timeout. Actions execute once. A then callback runs once; its assertion can observe the UI before the asynchronous update finishes. I use should for that assertion and then for a one-time transformation.
